  341 |     moves occur).

  350 |             destination path already exists, to copy the permissions

  369 |             recovery in some cases. Note that resumption is not

  371 |             the *part_file* exists.

   55 | def mkdir_p(path):
   56 |     """Creates a directory and any parent directories that may need to
   57 |     be created along the way, without raising errors for any existing
   58 |     directories. This function mimics the behavior of the ``mkdir -p``
   59 |     command available in Linux/BSD environments, but also works on
   60 |     Windows.
   61 |     """
   62 |     try:
   63 |         os.makedirs(path)
   64 |     except OSError as exc:
   65 |         if exc.errno == errno.EEXIST and os.path.isdir(path):
   66 |             return
   67 |         raise
   68 |     return

   71 | class FilePerms:
   72 |     """The :class:`FilePerms` type is used to represent standard POSIX
   73 |     filesystem permissions:
   74 | 
   75 |       * Read
   76 |       * Write
   77 |       * Execute
   78 | 
   79 |     Across three classes of user:
   80 | 
   81 |       * Owning (u)ser
   82 |       * Owner's (g)roup
   83 |       * Any (o)ther user
   84 | 
   85 |     This class assists with computing new permissions, as well as
   86 |     working with numeric octal ``777``-style and ``rwx``-style
   87 |     permissions. Currently it only considers the bottom 9 permission
   88 |     bits; it does not support sticky bits or more advanced permission
   89 |     systems.
   90 | 
   91 |     Args:
   92 |         user (str): A string in the 'rwx' format, omitting characters
   93 |             for which owning user's permissions are not provided.
   94 |         group (str): A string in the 'rwx' format, omitting characters
   95 |             for which owning group permissions are not provided.
   96 |         other (str): A string in the 'rwx' format, omitting characters
   97 |             for which owning other/world permissions are not provided.
   98 | 
   99 |     There are many ways to use :class:`FilePerms`:
  100 | 
  101 |     >>> FilePerms(user='rwx', group='xrw', other='wxr')  # note character order
  102 |     FilePerms(user='rwx', group='rwx', other='rwx')
  103 |     >>> int(FilePerms('r', 'r', ''))
  104 |     288
  105 |     >>> oct(288)[-3:]  # XXX Py3k
  106 |     '440'
  107 | 
  108 |     See also the :meth:`FilePerms.from_int` and
  109 |     :meth:`FilePerms.from_path` classmethods for useful alternative
  110 |     ways to construct :class:`FilePerms` objects.
  111 |     """
  112 |     # TODO: consider more than the lower 9 bits
  113 |     class _FilePermProperty:
  114 |         _perm_chars = 'rwx'
  115 |         _perm_set = frozenset('rwx')
  116 |         _perm_val = {'r': 4, 'w': 2, 'x': 1}  # for sorting
  117 | 
  118 |         def __init__(self, attribute, offset):
  119 |             self.attribute = attribute
  120 |             self.offset = offset
  121 | 
  122 |         def __get__(self, fp_obj, type_=None):
  123 |             if fp_obj is None:
  124 |                 return self
  125 |             return getattr(fp_obj, self.attribute)
  126 | 
  127 |         def __set__(self, fp_obj, value):
  128 |             cur = getattr(fp_obj, self.attribute)
  129 |             if cur == value:
  130 |                 return
  131 |             try:
  132 |                 invalid_chars = set(str(value)) - self._perm_set
  133 |             except TypeError:
  134 |                 raise TypeError('expected string, not %r' % value)
  135 |             if invalid_chars:
  136 |                 raise ValueError('got invalid chars %r in permission'
  137 |                                  ' specification %r, expected empty string'
  138 |                                  ' or one or more of %r'
  139 |                                  % (invalid_chars, value, self._perm_chars))
  140 | 
  141 |             def sort_key(c): return self._perm_val[c]
  142 |             new_value = ''.join(sorted(set(value),
  143 |                                        key=sort_key, reverse=True))
  144 |             setattr(fp_obj, self.attribute, new_value)
  145 |             self._update_integer(fp_obj, new_value)
  146 | 
  147 |         def _update_integer(self, fp_obj, value):
  148 |             mode = 0
  149 |             key = 'xwr'
  150 |             for symbol in value:
  151 |                 bit = 2 ** key.index(symbol)
  152 |                 mode |= (bit << (self.offset * 3))
  153 |             fp_obj._integer |= mode
  154 | 
  155 |     def __init__(self, user='', group='', other=''):
  156 |         self._user, self._group, self._other = '', '', ''
  157 |         self._integer = 0
  158 |         self.user = user
  159 |         self.group = group
  160 |         self.other = other
  161 | 
  162 |     @classmethod
  163 |     def from_int(cls, i):
  164 |         """Create a :class:`FilePerms` object from an integer.
  165 | 
  166 |         >>> FilePerms.from_int(0o644)  # note the leading zero-oh for octal
  167 |         FilePerms(user='rw', group='r', other='r')
  168 |         """
  169 |         i &= FULL_PERMS
  170 |         key = ('', 'x', 'w', 'xw', 'r', 'rx', 'rw', 'rwx')
  171 |         parts = []
  172 |         while i:
  173 |             parts.append(key[i & _SINGLE_FULL_PERM])
  174 |             i >>= 3
  175 |         parts.reverse()
  176 |         return cls(*parts)
  177 | 
  178 |     @classmethod
  179 |     def from_path(cls, path):
  180 |         """Make a new :class:`FilePerms` object based on the permissions
  181 |         assigned to the file or directory at *path*.
  182 | 
  183 |         Args:
  184 |             path (str): Filesystem path of the target file.
  185 | 
  186 |         Here's an example that holds true on most systems:
  187 | 
  188 |         >>> import tempfile
  189 |         >>> 'r' in FilePerms.from_path(tempfile.gettempdir()).user
  190 |         True
  191 |         """
  192 |         stat_res = os.stat(path)
  193 |         return cls.from_int(stat.S_IMODE(stat_res.st_mode))
  194 | 
  195 |     def __int__(self):
  196 |         return self._integer
  197 | 
  198 |     # Sphinx tip: attribute docstrings come after the attribute

  201 |     group = _FilePermProperty('_group', 1)
  202 |     "Stores the ``rwx``-formatted *group* permission."
  203 |     other = _FilePermProperty('_other', 0)
  204 |     "Stores the ``rwx``-formatted *other* permission."

  206 |     def __repr__(self):
  207 |         cn = self.__class__.__name__
  208 |         return ('%s(user=%r, group=%r, other=%r)'
  209 |                 % (cn, self.user, self.group, self.other))

  335 | class AtomicSaver:
  336 |     """``AtomicSaver`` is a configurable `context manager`_ that provides
  337 |     a writable :class:`file` which will be moved into place as long as
  338 |     no exceptions are raised within the context manager's block. These
  339 |     "part files" are created in the same directory as the destination
  340 |     path to ensure atomic move operations (i.e., no cross-filesystem
  341 |     moves occur).
  342 | 
  343 |     Args:
  344 |         dest_path (str): The path where the completed file will be
  345 |             written.
  346 |         overwrite (bool): Whether to overwrite the destination file if
  347 |             it exists at completion time. Defaults to ``True``.
  348 |         file_perms (int): Integer representation of file permissions
  349 |             for the newly-created file. Defaults are, when the
  350 |             destination path already exists, to copy the permissions
  351 |             from the previous file, or if the file did not exist, to
  352 |             respect the user's configured `umask`_, usually resulting
  353 |             in octal 0644 or 0664.
  354 |         text_mode (bool): Whether to open the destination file in text
  355 |             mode (i.e., ``'w'`` not ``'wb'``). Defaults to ``False`` (``wb``).
  356 |         part_file (str): Name of the temporary *part_file*. Defaults
  357 |             to *dest_path* + ``.part``. Note that this argument is
  358 |             just the filename, and not the full path of the part
  359 |             file. To guarantee atomic saves, part files are always
  360 |             created in the same directory as the destination path.
  361 |         overwrite_part (bool): Whether to overwrite the *part_file*,
  362 |             should it exist at setup time. Defaults to ``False``,
  363 |             which results in an :exc:`OSError` being raised on
  364 |             pre-existing part files. Be careful of setting this to
  365 |             ``True`` in situations when multiple threads or processes
  366 |             could be writing to the same part file.
  367 |         rm_part_on_exc (bool): Remove *part_file* on exception cases.
  368 |             Defaults to ``True``, but ``False`` can be useful for
  369 |             recovery in some cases. Note that resumption is not
  370 |             automatic and by default an :exc:`OSError` is raised if
  371 |             the *part_file* exists.
  372 | 
  373 |     Practically, the AtomicSaver serves a few purposes:
  374 | 
  375 |       * Avoiding overwriting an existing, valid file with a partially
  376 |         written one.
  377 |       * Providing a reasonable guarantee that a part file only has one
  378 |         writer at a time.
  379 |       * Optional recovery of partial data in failure cases.
  380 | 
  381 |     .. _context manager: https://docs.python.org/2/reference/compound_stmts.html#with
  382 |     .. _umask: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umask
  383 | 
  384 |     """
  385 |     _default_file_perms = RW_PERMS
  386 | 
  387 |     # TODO: option to abort if target file modify date has changed since start?
  388 |     def __init__(self, dest_path, **kwargs):
  389 |         self.dest_path = os.fspath(dest_path)
  390 |         self.overwrite = kwargs.pop('overwrite', True)
  391 |         self.file_perms = kwargs.pop('file_perms', None)
  392 |         self.overwrite_part = kwargs.pop('overwrite_part', False)
  393 |         self.part_filename = kwargs.pop('part_file', None)
  394 |         self.rm_part_on_exc = kwargs.pop('rm_part_on_exc', True)
  395 |         self.text_mode = kwargs.pop('text_mode', False)
  396 |         self.buffering = kwargs.pop('buffering', -1)
  397 |         if kwargs:
  398 |             raise TypeError(f'unexpected kwargs: {kwargs.keys()!r}')
  399 | 
  400 |         self.dest_path = os.path.abspath(self.dest_path)
  401 |         self.dest_dir = os.path.dirname(self.dest_path)
  402 |         if not self.part_filename:
  403 |             self.part_path = self.dest_path + '.part'
  404 |         else:
  405 |             self.part_path = os.path.join(self.dest_dir, self.part_filename)
  406 |         self.mode = 'w+' if self.text_mode else 'w+b'
  407 |         self.open_flags = _TEXT_OPENFLAGS if self.text_mode else _BIN_OPENFLAGS
  408 | 
  409 |         self.part_file = None
  410 | 
  411 |     def _open_part_file(self):
  412 |         do_chmod = True
  413 |         file_perms = self.file_perms
  414 |         if file_perms is None:
  415 |             try:
  416 |                 # try to copy from file being replaced
  417 |                 stat_res = os.stat(self.dest_path)
  418 |                 file_perms = stat.S_IMODE(stat_res.st_mode)
  419 |             except OSError:
  420 |                 # default if no destination file exists
  421 |                 file_perms = self._default_file_perms
  422 |                 do_chmod = False  # respect the umask
  423 | 
  424 |         fd = os.open(self.part_path, self.open_flags, file_perms)
  425 |         set_cloexec(fd)
  426 |         self.part_file = os.fdopen(fd, self.mode, self.buffering)
  427 | 
  428 |         # if default perms are overridden by the user or previous dest_path
  429 |         # chmod away the effects of the umask
  430 |         if do_chmod:
  431 |             try:
  432 |                 os.chmod(self.part_path, file_perms)
  433 |             except OSError:
  434 |                 self.part_file.close()
  435 |                 raise
  436 |         return

  438 |     def setup(self):
  439 |         """Called on context manager entry (the :keyword:`with` statement),
  440 |         the ``setup()`` method creates the temporary file in the same
  441 |         directory as the destination file.
  442 | 
  443 |         ``setup()`` tests for a writable directory with rename permissions
  444 |         early, as the part file may not be written to immediately (not
  445 |         using :func:`os.access` because of the potential issues of
  446 |         effective vs. real privileges).
  447 | 
  448 |         If the caller is not using the :class:`AtomicSaver` as a
  449 |         context manager, this method should be called explicitly
  450 |         before writing.
  451 |         """
  452 |         if os.path.lexists(self.dest_path):
  453 |             if not self.overwrite:
  454 |                 raise OSError(errno.EEXIST,
  455 |                               'Overwrite disabled and file already exists',
  456 |                               self.dest_path)
  457 |         if self.overwrite_part and os.path.lexists(self.part_path):
  458 |             os.unlink(self.part_path)
  459 |         self._open_part_file()
  460 |         return
  461 | 
  462 |     def __enter__(self):
  463 |         self.setup()
  464 |         return self.part_file
  465 | 
  466 |     def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
  467 |         if self.part_file:
  468 |             # Ensure data is flushed and synced to disk before closing
  469 |             self.part_file.flush()
  470 |             os.fsync(self.part_file.fileno())
  471 |             self.part_file.close()
  472 |         if exc_type:
  473 |             if self.rm_part_on_exc:
  474 |                 try:
  475 |                     os.unlink(self.part_path)
  476 |                 except Exception:
  477 |                     pass  # avoid masking original error
  478 |             return
  479 |         try:
  480 |             atomic_rename(self.part_path, self.dest_path,
  481 |                           overwrite=self.overwrite)
  482 |         except OSError:
  483 |             if self.rm_part_on_exc:
  484 |                 try:
  485 |                     os.unlink(self.part_path)
  486 |                 except Exception:
  487 |                     pass  # avoid masking original error
  488 |             raise  # could not save destination file
  489 |         return

  492 | def iter_find_files(directory, patterns, ignored=None, include_dirs=False, max_depth=None):
  493 |     """Returns a generator that yields file paths under a *directory*,
  494 |     matching *patterns* using `glob`_ syntax (e.g., ``*.txt``). Also
  495 |     supports *ignored* patterns.
  496 | 
  497 |     Args:
  498 |         directory (str): Path that serves as the root of the
  499 |             search. Yielded paths will include this as a prefix.
  500 |         patterns (str or list): A single pattern or list of
  501 |             glob-formatted patterns to find under *directory*.
  502 |         ignored (str or list): A single pattern or list of
  503 |             glob-formatted patterns to ignore.
  504 |         include_dirs (bool): Whether to include directories that match
  505 |            patterns, as well. Defaults to ``False``.
  506 |         max_depth (int): traverse up to this level of subdirectory.
  507 |            I.e., 0 for the specified *directory* only, 1 for *directory* 
  508 |            and one level of subdirectory.
  509 | 
  510 |     For example, finding Python files in the current directory:
  511 | 
  512 |     >>> _CUR_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
  513 |     >>> filenames = sorted(iter_find_files(_CUR_DIR, '*.py'))
  514 |     >>> os.path.basename(filenames[-1])
  515 |     'urlutils.py'
  516 | 
  517 |     Or, Python files while ignoring emacs lockfiles:
  518 | 
  519 |     >>> filenames = iter_find_files(_CUR_DIR, '*.py', ignored='.#*')
  520 | 
  521 |     .. _glob: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glob_%28programming%29
  522 | 
  523 |     """
  524 |     if isinstance(patterns, str):
  525 |         patterns = [patterns]
  526 |     pats_re = re.compile('|'.join([fnmatch.translate(p) for p in patterns]))
  527 | 
  528 |     if not ignored:
  529 |         ignored = []
  530 |     elif isinstance(ignored, str):
  531 |         ignored = [ignored]
  532 |     ign_re = re.compile('|'.join([fnmatch.translate(p) for p in ignored]))
  533 |     directory = os.fspath(directory)
  534 |     start_depth = len(directory.split(os.path.sep))
  535 |     for root, dirs, files in os.walk(directory):
  536 |         if max_depth is not None and (len(root.split(os.path.sep)) - start_depth) > max_depth:
  537 |             continue
  538 |         if include_dirs:
  539 |             for basename in dirs:
  540 |                 if pats_re.match(basename):
  541 |                     if ignored and ign_re.match(basename):
  542 |                         continue
  543 |                     filename = os.path.join(root, basename)
  544 |                     yield filename
  545 | 
  546 |         for basename in files:
  547 |             if pats_re.match(basename):
  548 |                 if ignored and ign_re.match(basename):
  549 |                     continue
  550 |                 filename = os.path.join(root, basename)
  551 |                 yield filename
  552 |     return

  555 | def copy_tree(src, dst, symlinks=False, ignore=None):
  556 |     """The ``copy_tree`` function is an exact copy of the built-in
  557 |     :func:`shutil.copytree`, with one key difference: it will not
  558 |     raise an exception if part of the tree already exists. It achieves
  559 |     this by using :func:`mkdir_p`.
  560 | 
  561 |     As of Python 3.8, you may pass :func:`shutil.copytree` the
  562 |     `dirs_exist_ok=True` flag to achieve the same effect.
  563 | 
  564 |     Args:
  565 |         src (str): Path of the source directory to copy.
  566 |         dst (str): Destination path. Existing directories accepted.
  567 |         symlinks (bool): If ``True``, copy symlinks rather than their
  568 |             contents.
  569 |         ignore (callable): A callable that takes a path and directory
  570 |             listing, returning the files within the listing to be ignored.
  571 | 
  572 |     For more details, check out :func:`shutil.copytree` and
  573 |     :func:`shutil.copy2`.
  574 | 
  575 |     """
  576 |     names = os.listdir(src)
  577 |     if ignore is not None:
  578 |         ignored_names = ignore(src, names)
  579 |     else:
  580 |         ignored_names = set()
  581 | 
  582 |     mkdir_p(dst)

   55 | def mkdir_p(path):
   56 |     """Creates a directory and any parent directories that may need to
   57 |     be created along the way, without raising errors for any existing
   58 |     directories. This function mimics the behavior of the ``mkdir -p``
   59 |     command available in Linux/BSD environments, but also works on
   60 |     Windows.
   61 |     """
   62 |     try:
   63 |         os.makedirs(path)
   64 |     except OSError as exc:
   65 |         if exc.errno == errno.EEXIST and os.path.isdir(path):
   66 |             return
   67 |         raise
   68 |     return

   71 | class FilePerms:
   72 |     """The :class:`FilePerms` type is used to represent standard POSIX
   73 |     filesystem permissions:
   74 | 
   75 |       * Read
   76 |       * Write
   77 |       * Execute
   78 | 
   79 |     Across three classes of user:
   80 | 
   81 |       * Owning (u)ser
   82 |       * Owner's (g)roup
   83 |       * Any (o)ther user
   84 | 
   85 |     This class assists with computing new permissions, as well as
   86 |     working with numeric octal ``777``-style and ``rwx``-style
   87 |     permissions. Currently it only considers the bottom 9 permission
   88 |     bits; it does not support sticky bits or more advanced permission
   89 |     systems.
   90 | 
   91 |     Args:
   92 |         user (str): A string in the 'rwx' format, omitting characters
   93 |             for which owning user's permissions are not provided.
   94 |         group (str): A string in the 'rwx' format, omitting characters
   95 |             for which owning group permissions are not provided.
   96 |         other (str): A string in the 'rwx' format, omitting characters
   97 |             for which owning other/world permissions are not provided.
   98 | 
   99 |     There are many ways to use :class:`FilePerms`:
  100 | 
  101 |     >>> FilePerms(user='rwx', group='xrw', other='wxr')  # note character order
  102 |     FilePerms(user='rwx', group='rwx', other='rwx')
  103 |     >>> int(FilePerms('r', 'r', ''))
  104 |     288
  105 |     >>> oct(288)[-3:]  # XXX Py3k
  106 |     '440'
  107 | 
  108 |     See also the :meth:`FilePerms.from_int` and
  109 |     :meth:`FilePerms.from_path` classmethods for useful alternative
  110 |     ways to construct :class:`FilePerms` objects.
  111 |     """
  112 |     # TODO: consider more than the lower 9 bits
  113 |     class _FilePermProperty:
  114 |         _perm_chars = 'rwx'
  115 |         _perm_set = frozenset('rwx')
  116 |         _perm_val = {'r': 4, 'w': 2, 'x': 1}  # for sorting
  117 | 
  118 |         def __init__(self, attribute, offset):
  119 |             self.attribute = attribute
  120 |             self.offset = offset
  121 | 
  122 |         def __get__(self, fp_obj, type_=None):
  123 |             if fp_obj is None:
  124 |                 return self
  125 |             return getattr(fp_obj, self.attribute)
  126 | 
  127 |         def __set__(self, fp_obj, value):
  128 |             cur = getattr(fp_obj, self.attribute)
  129 |             if cur == value:
  130 |                 return
  131 |             try:
  132 |                 invalid_chars = set(str(value)) - self._perm_set
  133 |             except TypeError:
  134 |                 raise TypeError('expected string, not %r' % value)
  135 |             if invalid_chars:
  136 |                 raise ValueError('got invalid chars %r in permission'
  137 |                                  ' specification %r, expected empty string'
  138 |                                  ' or one or more of %r'
  139 |                                  % (invalid_chars, value, self._perm_chars))
  140 | 
  141 |             def sort_key(c): return self._perm_val[c]
  142 |             new_value = ''.join(sorted(set(value),
  143 |                                        key=sort_key, reverse=True))
  144 |             setattr(fp_obj, self.attribute, new_value)
  145 |             self._update_integer(fp_obj, new_value)
  146 | 
  147 |         def _update_integer(self, fp_obj, value):
  148 |             mode = 0
  149 |             key = 'xwr'
  150 |             for symbol in value:
  151 |                 bit = 2 ** key.index(symbol)
  152 |                 mode |= (bit << (self.offset * 3))
  153 |             fp_obj._integer |= mode
  154 | 
  155 |     def __init__(self, user='', group='', other=''):
  156 |         self._user, self._group, self._other = '', '', ''
  157 |         self._integer = 0
  158 |         self.user = user
  159 |         self.group = group
  160 |         self.other = other
  161 | 
  162 |     @classmethod
  163 |     def from_int(cls, i):
  164 |         """Create a :class:`FilePerms` object from an integer.
  165 | 
  166 |         >>> FilePerms.from_int(0o644)  # note the leading zero-oh for octal
  167 |         FilePerms(user='rw', group='r', other='r')
  168 |         """
  169 |         i &= FULL_PERMS
  170 |         key = ('', 'x', 'w', 'xw', 'r', 'rx', 'rw', 'rwx')
  171 |         parts = []
  172 |         while i:
  173 |             parts.append(key[i & _SINGLE_FULL_PERM])
  174 |             i >>= 3
  175 |         parts.reverse()
  176 |         return cls(*parts)
  177 | 
  178 |     @classmethod
  179 |     def from_path(cls, path):
  180 |         """Make a new :class:`FilePerms` object based on the permissions
  181 |         assigned to the file or directory at *path*.
  182 | 
  183 |         Args:
  184 |             path (str): Filesystem path of the target file.
  185 | 
  186 |         Here's an example that holds true on most systems:
  187 | 
  188 |         >>> import tempfile
  189 |         >>> 'r' in FilePerms.from_path(tempfile.gettempdir()).user
  190 |         True
  191 |         """
  192 |         stat_res = os.stat(path)
  193 |         return cls.from_int(stat.S_IMODE(stat_res.st_mode))
  194 | 
  195 |     def __int__(self):
  196 |         return self._integer
  197 | 
  198 |     # Sphinx tip: attribute docstrings come after the attribute

  201 |     group = _FilePermProperty('_group', 1)
  202 |     "Stores the ``rwx``-formatted *group* permission."
  203 |     other = _FilePermProperty('_other', 0)
  204 |     "Stores the ``rwx``-formatted *other* permission."

  206 |     def __repr__(self):
  207 |         cn = self.__class__.__name__
  208 |         return ('%s(user=%r, group=%r, other=%r)'
  209 |                 % (cn, self.user, self.group, self.other))

  335 | class AtomicSaver:
  336 |     """``AtomicSaver`` is a configurable `context manager`_ that provides
  337 |     a writable :class:`file` which will be moved into place as long as
  338 |     no exceptions are raised within the context manager's block. These
  339 |     "part files" are created in the same directory as the destination
  340 |     path to ensure atomic move operations (i.e., no cross-filesystem
  341 |     moves occur).
  342 | 
  343 |     Args:
  344 |         dest_path (str): The path where the completed file will be
  345 |             written.
  346 |         overwrite (bool): Whether to overwrite the destination file if
  347 |             it exists at completion time. Defaults to ``True``.
  348 |         file_perms (int): Integer representation of file permissions
  349 |             for the newly-created file. Defaults are, when the
  350 |             destination path already exists, to copy the permissions
  351 |             from the previous file, or if the file did not exist, to
  352 |             respect the user's configured `umask`_, usually resulting
  353 |             in octal 0644 or 0664.
  354 |         text_mode (bool): Whether to open the destination file in text
  355 |             mode (i.e., ``'w'`` not ``'wb'``). Defaults to ``False`` (``wb``).
  356 |         part_file (str): Name of the temporary *part_file*. Defaults
  357 |             to *dest_path* + ``.part``. Note that this argument is
  358 |             just the filename, and not the full path of the part
  359 |             file. To guarantee atomic saves, part files are always
  360 |             created in the same directory as the destination path.
  361 |         overwrite_part (bool): Whether to overwrite the *part_file*,
  362 |             should it exist at setup time. Defaults to ``False``,
  363 |             which results in an :exc:`OSError` being raised on
  364 |             pre-existing part files. Be careful of setting this to
  365 |             ``True`` in situations when multiple threads or processes
  366 |             could be writing to the same part file.
  367 |         rm_part_on_exc (bool): Remove *part_file* on exception cases.
  368 |             Defaults to ``True``, but ``False`` can be useful for
  369 |             recovery in some cases. Note that resumption is not
  370 |             automatic and by default an :exc:`OSError` is raised if
  371 |             the *part_file* exists.
  372 | 
  373 |     Practically, the AtomicSaver serves a few purposes:
  374 | 
  375 |       * Avoiding overwriting an existing, valid file with a partially
  376 |         written one.
  377 |       * Providing a reasonable guarantee that a part file only has one
  378 |         writer at a time.
  379 |       * Optional recovery of partial data in failure cases.
  380 | 
  381 |     .. _context manager: https://docs.python.org/2/reference/compound_stmts.html#with
  382 |     .. _umask: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umask
  383 | 
  384 |     """
  385 |     _default_file_perms = RW_PERMS
  386 | 
  387 |     # TODO: option to abort if target file modify date has changed since start?
  388 |     def __init__(self, dest_path, **kwargs):
  389 |         self.dest_path = os.fspath(dest_path)
  390 |         self.overwrite = kwargs.pop('overwrite', True)
  391 |         self.file_perms = kwargs.pop('file_perms', None)
  392 |         self.overwrite_part = kwargs.pop('overwrite_part', False)
  393 |         self.part_filename = kwargs.pop('part_file', None)
  394 |         self.rm_part_on_exc = kwargs.pop('rm_part_on_exc', True)
  395 |         self.text_mode = kwargs.pop('text_mode', False)
  396 |         self.buffering = kwargs.pop('buffering', -1)
  397 |         if kwargs:
  398 |             raise TypeError(f'unexpected kwargs: {kwargs.keys()!r}')
  399 | 
  400 |         self.dest_path = os.path.abspath(self.dest_path)
  401 |         self.dest_dir = os.path.dirname(self.dest_path)
  402 |         if not self.part_filename:
  403 |             self.part_path = self.dest_path + '.part'
  404 |         else:
  405 |             self.part_path = os.path.join(self.dest_dir, self.part_filename)
  406 |         self.mode = 'w+' if self.text_mode else 'w+b'
  407 |         self.open_flags = _TEXT_OPENFLAGS if self.text_mode else _BIN_OPENFLAGS
  408 | 
  409 |         self.part_file = None
  410 | 
  411 |     def _open_part_file(self):
  412 |         do_chmod = True
  413 |         file_perms = self.file_perms
  414 |         if file_perms is None:
  415 |             try:
  416 |                 # try to copy from file being replaced
  417 |                 stat_res = os.stat(self.dest_path)
  418 |                 file_perms = stat.S_IMODE(stat_res.st_mode)
  419 |             except OSError:
  420 |                 # default if no destination file exists
  421 |                 file_perms = self._default_file_perms
  422 |                 do_chmod = False  # respect the umask
  423 | 
  424 |         fd = os.open(self.part_path, self.open_flags, file_perms)
  425 |         set_cloexec(fd)
  426 |         self.part_file = os.fdopen(fd, self.mode, self.buffering)
  427 | 
  428 |         # if default perms are overridden by the user or previous dest_path
  429 |         # chmod away the effects of the umask
  430 |         if do_chmod:
  431 |             try:
  432 |                 os.chmod(self.part_path, file_perms)
  433 |             except OSError:
  434 |                 self.part_file.close()
  435 |                 raise
  436 |         return

  438 |     def setup(self):
  439 |         """Called on context manager entry (the :keyword:`with` statement),
  440 |         the ``setup()`` method creates the temporary file in the same
  441 |         directory as the destination file.
  442 | 
  443 |         ``setup()`` tests for a writable directory with rename permissions
  444 |         early, as the part file may not be written to immediately (not
  445 |         using :func:`os.access` because of the potential issues of
  446 |         effective vs. real privileges).
  447 | 
  448 |         If the caller is not using the :class:`AtomicSaver` as a
  449 |         context manager, this method should be called explicitly
  450 |         before writing.
  451 |         """
  452 |         if os.path.lexists(self.dest_path):
  453 |             if not self.overwrite:
  454 |                 raise OSError(errno.EEXIST,
  455 |                               'Overwrite disabled and file already exists',
  456 |                               self.dest_path)
  457 |         if self.overwrite_part and os.path.lexists(self.part_path):
  458 |             os.unlink(self.part_path)
  459 |         self._open_part_file()
  460 |         return
  461 | 
  462 |     def __enter__(self):
  463 |         self.setup()
  464 |         return self.part_file
  465 | 
  466 |     def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
  467 |         if self.part_file:
  468 |             # Ensure data is flushed and synced to disk before closing
  469 |             self.part_file.flush()
  470 |             os.fsync(self.part_file.fileno())
  471 |             self.part_file.close()
  472 |         if exc_type:
  473 |             if self.rm_part_on_exc:
  474 |                 try:
  475 |                     os.unlink(self.part_path)
  476 |                 except Exception:
  477 |                     pass  # avoid masking original error
  478 |             return
  479 |         try:
  480 |             atomic_rename(self.part_path, self.dest_path,
  481 |                           overwrite=self.overwrite)
  482 |         except OSError:
  483 |             if self.rm_part_on_exc:
  484 |                 try:
  485 |                     os.unlink(self.part_path)
  486 |                 except Exception:
  487 |                     pass  # avoid masking original error
  488 |             raise  # could not save destination file
  489 |         return

  492 | def iter_find_files(directory, patterns, ignored=None, include_dirs=False, max_depth=None):
  493 |     """Returns a generator that yields file paths under a *directory*,
  494 |     matching *patterns* using `glob`_ syntax (e.g., ``*.txt``). Also
  495 |     supports *ignored* patterns.
  496 | 
  497 |     Args:
  498 |         directory (str): Path that serves as the root of the
  499 |             search. Yielded paths will include this as a prefix.
  500 |         patterns (str or list): A single pattern or list of
  501 |             glob-formatted patterns to find under *directory*.
  502 |         ignored (str or list): A single pattern or list of
  503 |             glob-formatted patterns to ignore.
  504 |         include_dirs (bool): Whether to include directories that match
  505 |            patterns, as well. Defaults to ``False``.
  506 |         max_depth (int): traverse up to this level of subdirectory.
  507 |            I.e., 0 for the specified *directory* only, 1 for *directory* 
  508 |            and one level of subdirectory.
  509 | 
  510 |     For example, finding Python files in the current directory:
  511 | 
  512 |     >>> _CUR_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
  513 |     >>> filenames = sorted(iter_find_files(_CUR_DIR, '*.py'))
  514 |     >>> os.path.basename(filenames[-1])
  515 |     'urlutils.py'
  516 | 
  517 |     Or, Python files while ignoring emacs lockfiles:
  518 | 
  519 |     >>> filenames = iter_find_files(_CUR_DIR, '*.py', ignored='.#*')
  520 | 
  521 |     .. _glob: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glob_%28programming%29
  522 | 
  523 |     """
  524 |     if isinstance(patterns, str):
  525 |         patterns = [patterns]
  526 |     pats_re = re.compile('|'.join([fnmatch.translate(p) for p in patterns]))
  527 | 
  528 |     if not ignored:
  529 |         ignored = []
  530 |     elif isinstance(ignored, str):
  531 |         ignored = [ignored]
  532 |     ign_re = re.compile('|'.join([fnmatch.translate(p) for p in ignored]))
  533 |     directory = os.fspath(directory)
  534 |     start_depth = len(directory.split(os.path.sep))
  535 |     for root, dirs, files in os.walk(directory):
  536 |         if max_depth is not None and (len(root.split(os.path.sep)) - start_depth) > max_depth:
  537 |             continue
  538 |         if include_dirs:
  539 |             for basename in dirs:
  540 |                 if pats_re.match(basename):
  541 |                     if ignored and ign_re.match(basename):
  542 |                         continue
  543 |                     filename = os.path.join(root, basename)
  544 |                     yield filename
  545 | 
  546 |         for basename in files:
  547 |             if pats_re.match(basename):
  548 |                 if ignored and ign_re.match(basename):
  549 |                     continue
  550 |                 filename = os.path.join(root, basename)
  551 |                 yield filename
  552 |     return

  555 | def copy_tree(src, dst, symlinks=False, ignore=None):
  556 |     """The ``copy_tree`` function is an exact copy of the built-in
  557 |     :func:`shutil.copytree`, with one key difference: it will not
  558 |     raise an exception if part of the tree already exists. It achieves
  559 |     this by using :func:`mkdir_p`.
  560 | 
  561 |     As of Python 3.8, you may pass :func:`shutil.copytree` the
  562 |     `dirs_exist_ok=True` flag to achieve the same effect.
  563 | 
  564 |     Args:
  565 |         src (str): Path of the source directory to copy.
  566 |         dst (str): Destination path. Existing directories accepted.
  567 |         symlinks (bool): If ``True``, copy symlinks rather than their
  568 |             contents.
  569 |         ignore (callable): A callable that takes a path and directory
  570 |             listing, returning the files within the listing to be ignored.
  571 | 
  572 |     For more details, check out :func:`shutil.copytree` and
  573 |     :func:`shutil.copy2`.
  574 | 
  575 |     """
  576 |     names = os.listdir(src)
  577 |     if ignore is not None:
  578 |         ignored_names = ignore(src, names)
  579 |     else:
  580 |         ignored_names = set()
  581 | 
  582 |     mkdir_p(dst)

    (root / "a.txt").write_text("a")
    (root / "b.py").write_text("b")
    sub = root / "sub"
    sub.mkdir()
    (sub / "c.txt").write_text("c")
    (sub / "d.py").write_text("d")
    sub2 = sub / "deep"

    (sub2 / "e.txt").write_text("e")
    return root

  695 | def rotate_file(filename, *, keep: int = 5):
  696 |     """

  698 |     with all conflicting filenames being moved up by one, dropping any files beyond *keep*.

  705 |         raise ValueError(f'expected "keep" to be >=1, not {keep}')
  706 |     if not os.path.exists(filename):

  708 |     if not os.path.isfile(filename):
  709 |         raise ValueError(f'expected {filename} to be a file')
  710 |

  712 |     kept_names = []
  713 |     for i in range(1, keep + 1):

  716 |         else:
